statement: In a meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials of medications for methamphetamine or amphetamine withdrawal searched to December 2020 (nine trials of six medications, about 240 participants, six trials at high risk of bias), only six trials of four medications could be pooled; the ibudilast and varenicline trials and one modafinil trial gave no usable data on the review's outcomes. No pooled medication other than amineptine differed from placebo on any pooled outcome: discontinuation with any medication RR 0.70 (95% CI 0.40–1.23); with mirtazapine RR 0.96 (0.48–1.92); withdrawal-symptom scores SMD 0.17 (−0.43 to 0.77); global state (overall severity ratings, three trials), no significant difference. Amineptine, tested in two small trials by the same three investigators, may have reduced discontinuation (RR 0.22, 0.07–0.72; very low certainty; the authors write that it 'may reduce' discontinuation) and improved global state (two trials, 72 participants; low certainty by the review's rating), although the review prints its global-state figures in two inconsistent versions; according to the review it was withdrawn from the market in 1999 after reports of liver toxicity and non-medical use, and the two case reports cited for this predate the stated year. Outside the pooled outcomes, single small trials reported less fatigue on amantadine, faster visual reaction time but no other cognitive benefit on varenicline, and better scores on 2 of 12 measures of a sustained-attention test on ibudilast, while two mirtazapine trials found no benefit for sleep, one reporting more night awakenings than placebo. Only one trial reported adverse events by arm. The two mirtazapine trials here treated the withdrawal period, over two weeks; they are different from the longer trials of mirtazapine for methamphetamine dependence.
plain: Nine small trials have tested six medicines for meth or amphetamine withdrawal, the low mood, tiredness, sleep changes and craving after stopping. Only six of them, testing four medicines, could be combined. Of those medicines, none clearly helped compared with a placebo, apart from one drug that is no longer sold. Single trials reported a few narrower effects, such as less tiredness on amantadine, and one found more waking at night on mirtazapine. The trials were so few, small and flawed that a benefit cannot be ruled out either, and the medicines' side effects were rarely reported. These short mirtazapine trials are separate from the longer trials of mirtazapine for meth use.
population: People with a DSM or ICD diagnosis of methamphetamine or amphetamine use disorder or withdrawal, in inpatient, residential, laboratory, outpatient and one probation-centre setting (USA, Thailand, Australia, Iran); in four trials both arms also received an adjunctive treatment (low-dose lorazepam with supportive care in the two amineptine trials, counselling or symptomatic therapy in two others)
exposure: Mirtazapine, modafinil, amineptine, amantadine, ibudilast or varenicline
outcome: Discontinuation; global state; withdrawal symptoms; craving; adverse events
magnitude: Discontinuation, any medication RR 0.70 (0.40–1.23), 6 trials, 186 participants; mirtazapine 0.96 (0.48–1.92); modafinil 0.67 (0.22–2.03); amantadine 1.33 (0.34–5.24); amineptine 0.22 (0.07–0.72), 2 trials by the same three investigators, I² 58%; per-arm discontinuation counts appear only in the supplementary forest plots (not read), so no absolute effect can be given. Global state, 3 trials, 103 participants: any medication −0.24 (−0.73 to 0.25) and amineptine −0.49 (−0.80 to −0.17), labelled mean differences in the review's table and abstract; its text gives standardised mean differences of −0.34 (−1.06 to 0.25) and −0.70 (−1.18 to −0.22) instead, and the table's single-trial mirtazapine value lies outside its own interval. Withdrawal symptoms SMD 0.17 (−0.43 to 0.77), 3 trials, 93 participants. Craving SMD 0.34 (−0.77 to 1.45), 2 trials, 48 participants.

grade.reasoning: Randomized trials, but six of nine at high risk of bias (selective reporting in six, randomization concerns in five), and very serious imprecision: one or two trials of 19 to 74 participants per medication, with intervals compatible with large benefit and harm. Publication bias was not assessed by the review and cannot be excluded. The amineptine result rests on two small trials from one group, and its global-state estimate is printed as a mean difference in the abstract and table and as a different standardised mean difference in the text, beside a table value that lies outside its own interval, so its size is uncertain. Status mixed: the two mirtazapine trials point different ways (one of them, pooled for discontinuation, reported lower withdrawal scores in data the review could not pool), and amineptine differs from the other drugs.

changelog.change: Drafted from the first-pass study card(s); held until the references are built from Crossref and the cards are second-read.
Round 2 second reading: 'reduced' replaced by the authors' 'may reduce'; the market-withdrawal date attributed to the review, whose cited sources predate it.

Review round 2 (group P): the statement now says that only six of the nine trials, of four medications, could be pooled (the ibudilast and varenicline trials and one modafinil trial could not); adds the global-state outcome, including amineptine's improvement (rated low certainty by the review), with the caveat that the review prints these figures in two inconsistent versions (the methodologist's reading of them as the same result printed twice was not adopted); names the shared authorship of the two amineptine trials; reports the unpooled single-trial findings in both directions (the methodologist listed only the favourable ones); and distinguishes the two short withdrawal trials of mirtazapine from the longer dependence trials. Magnitude gives both versions of the global-state figures, the amineptine heterogeneity (I² 58%) and why no absolute effect can be given; population names the probation-centre setting and the adjunctive treatments given to both arms in four trials. In the reasoning, 'one unpooled trial' made precise: that mirtazapine trial was pooled for discontinuation, and only its withdrawal scores could not be pooled. Three anchors added from the saved full text. The methodologist confirmed anchors 0 to 6 at the stated place (recorded, METHODS §5.6).
